From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@finco.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinCo 	6 Performance SLO & context window follow-up

Alex  looping in Sean to answer the technical bits. Sean  quick background: FinCo needs a PoC to validate p50/p95 for three context profiles (4k/16k/32k), with streaming and two operating modes (latency-optimized vs cost-optimized). They care about time-to-first-token (TTFT) and end-to-end completion.

Sean here  TL;DR answers up front, details below.

- Can measure TTFT + time-to-last-token in the matrix. TTFT is primarily driven by model decoding latency and any initial kernel scheduling/host-device transfer; streaming typically reveals the first token much faster than waiting for full decode.
- Context window impact: latency scales roughly linearly with number of input tokens that must be attended to (and nonlinearly when KV cache management triggers). For our current optimized runtimes: 
  * 4k context: baseline p95 completion times are low (example: 120350ms at modest outputs, single concurrency).
  * 16k context: p95 increases  expect ~23x of 4k numbers for completion when not streaming; TTFT remains closer to baseline if we can stream early partial outputs.
  * 32k context: significant tail impact  p95 can approach multiple seconds under heavy decoding and naive batching. With optimized kernel selection, prefix caching, and streaming we can keep TTFT within ~400800ms for many cases, but completion times vary with output size and concurrency.

- Output tokens: decoding cost scales with output length; a 350-token completion will add ~x ms per token depending on batch/quantization. Well include token-per-second decode rates in the deliverable.

- Batching & concurrency: batching improves throughput and reduces cost but increases per-request latency (especially at low concurrency). For your PoC we can test both: 
  * Latency-optimized: minimal batching, priority scheduling, target p95 goals (higher cost).
  * Cost-optimized: larger batching windows, higher throughput at expense of higher tail latency.

- Streaming behavior: enabling chunked streaming (server-sent events / chunked HTTP) reduces perceived latency drastically by surfacing the first token earlier. Implementation-wise we avoid heavy buffering and send tokens as they are decoded; the penalty vs non-streaming is minimal if we reserve small decode windows and prioritize early tokens.

Proposed PoC test matrix (well run and report p50/p95/p99 + TTFT):
- Contexts: 4k / 16k / 32k (input+output)
- Output sizes: 60 tokens (median), 200 tokens (common), 350 tokens (95th)
- Concurrency: 1, 50, 200
- Modes: latency-optimized, cost-optimized
- Metrics reported: TTFT, completion time, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and p50/p95/p99 for each cell

Next steps I propose:
1) We provision a sandbox cluster and give you an API key by EOD Friday.
2) You provide a sample of representative transcripts (redacted) and expected output lengths.
3) Run the PoC (2 weeks) and then review the SLA doc (attached: sla_draft_v1.docx).

Notes/assumptions:
- For 32k context tests we'll recommend using a quantized model variant and enable prefix/KV caching for repeated historical retrievals  otherwise costs and latency grow quickly.
- If FinCo requires strict p99 contractual SLAs under bursty conditions, we should plan for Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) rather than shared hosted, since tail latency on shared pools is harder to guarantee.

Attachments: sla_draft_v1.docx

Happy to hop on a call to walk through the matrix; Sean and I are available Wed/Thu afternoon.

 Sean Gallagher
